name: Bouncer
summary: Email-list verification sold as credits that never expire, with a minimum purchase and a lower rate per 1,000 at higher volume. Unknowns and duplicates are not charged. Treat 'accept-all' domain results as unverified.
best_for: email marketers and outbound teams that clean lists regularly and want accurate verification with fair credit mechanics (no expiry, no double-charging)
skip_if: you send rarely to a stable opt-in list (occasional pay-as-you-go beats any subscription), or your problem is content/reputation rather than list hygiene
honest_knock: Not charging for unknowns and duplicates is genuinely fair — many rivals do. The honest framing for any verifier: it removes invalid addresses, which protects deliverability, but it can't make a cold list warm or a purchased list legitimate. Verify before every big send (lists decay measurably per month), and treat 'accept-all' domain results as the gamble they are, not as verified.

pricing.notes: Email verification credits, pay-as-you-go and never expiring (re-verified 2026-09-11): $8 per 1,000 credits is the minimum purchase. Volume brings the rate down to $35 per 5,000, $60 per 10,000 and $250 per 50,000. Above that it runs $400 per 100,000, $750 per 250,000, $1,250 per 500,000 and $2,000 per 1,000,000 - about $2 per 1,000 at the top volume, with anything above a million quoted by sales. The same calculator offers a monthly-subscription mode for verification that Bouncer states is discounted against pay-as-you-go; it publishes no fixed monthly tiers, so price it at your own volume. 100 free credits to test; duplicates and 'unknown' results aren't charged. The $25/$125/$250 per month tiers are the separate Deliverability Kit and now carry published allowances - 250, 1,000 and 2,500 test emails and 10, 25 and 50 IPs or domains monitored, with an unlimited Enterprise tier on quote. Shield is a separate real-time product laddered by monthly checks: $2 for 1,000, $20 for 10,000, $300 for 250,000 and $1,050 for 1,000,000.
